extractions.description: An empirical pancreatic-cancer and beta-cell study combining mouse and cell experiments with sequencing and machine-learning analysis of single-cell transcriptomic and epigenomic data.

type.quote: We performed scRNA-seq of isolated islet cells from aged-matched congenic (C57/B6) male wild-type (WT), moderately obese HFD-fed, and severely obese Lepob/ob mice
type.justification: The paper reports newly performed experiments and quantitative analyses of generated and published data.

name.quote: Pancreatic cancer, obesity, islets, beta cells, diabetes, ER stress, cholecystokinin
name.justification: The keywords and study claims directly identify pancreatic cancer as an addressed field.

name.quote: Pancreatic endocrine-exocrine crosstalk plays a key role in normal physiology and disease.
name.justification: The paper directly advances understanding of pancreatic endocrine-exocrine signaling.

name.quote: Our study also provides new insights into the cellular and molecular mechanisms that govern β cell adaptation to obesity
name.justification: The study makes direct claims about beta-cell biology and adaptation.

name.quote: Leveraging single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of multiple congenic obesity models and a suite of new machine learning-based computational tools
name.justification: Single-cell transcriptomics and computational analysis are central analytical fields in the paper.

name.quote: a suite of new machine learning-based computational tools for in silico lineage tracing (TrajectoryNet), latent-space archetypal analysis (AAnet), batch integration across datasets (scMMGAN), and optimal-transport distance-preserving embedding of patient data (DiffusionEMD)
name.justification: Machine learning is used as the computational setting rather than introduced as a new method in this paper.

name.quote: The obesity progression in mouse latent-space archetypal analysis correlates with type 2 diabetes in humans and mice.
name.justification: The paper analyzes and makes cross-species claims concerning type 2 diabetes.

name.quote: we next investigated how obesity, a pro-tumorigenic host metabolic state, modulates β cells to drive tumorigenesis
